pharm: Irreversibly inhibits the gastric H+/K+ ATPase (proton pump) at the parietal cell secretory surface, blocking the final step of gastric acid secretion.

summary: Rabeprazole is a substituted-benzimidazole proton pump inhibitor for healing and maintenance of erosive GERD, symptomatic GERD, duodenal ulcers, H. pylori eradication, and pathological hypersecretory conditions. It is contraindicated with rilpivirine and carries class risks of long-term acid suppression.
indications: Healing of erosive or ulcerative GERD (adults)
Maintenance of healing of erosive or ulcerative GERD (adults)
Treatment of symptomatic GERD (adults and adolescents >=12 years)
H. pylori eradication to reduce risk of duodenal ulcer recurrence (adults)
Pathological hypersecretory conditions including Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (adults)

dosage.t: 4 to 8 weeks (may extend additional 8 weeks if unhealed)

dosage.n: Adolescents >=12 yrs: 20 mg once daily up to 8 weeks

dosage.d: 20 mg once daily after morning meal
Rabeprazole 20 mg + amoxicillin 1000 mg + clarithromycin 500 mg, all twice daily
dosage.n: Take with morning and evening meals

dosage.d: Start 60 mg once daily, then titrate to need
dosage.n: Doses up to 100 mg/day or 60 mg twice daily used

admin: Swallow delayed-release tablets whole; do not chew, crush, or split
Duodenal ulcer: take after the morning meal
H. pylori regimen: take with food

Maintain full course even if symptoms improve
moa: Rabeprazole is a substituted-benzimidazole PPI. In the acidic environment of the parietal cell, it is protonated and converted to an active sulfenamide that covalently and irreversibly inhibits the gastric H+/K+ ATPase, the terminal step in acid secretion. New enzyme synthesis is required to restore acid output.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to rabeprazole, substituted benzimidazoles, or formulation components
Contraindications of clarithromycin/amoxicillin apply when used in combination
relative: Long-term high-dose therapy (fracture, hypomagnesemia, B12 deficiency risks)
Concomitant drugs requiring gastric acidity for absorption

preg: No adequate human data. Animal reproduction studies showed no adverse developmental effects at 8-13 times human AUC. Use only if clearly needed.
lact: No human lactation data; rabeprazole is present in rat milk. Weigh developmental/health benefits of breastfeeding against maternal need and potential infant effects.
renal: No dosage adjustment required in renal impairment.
hepatic: Use caution in severe hepatic impairment; clearance is reduced and exposure increased. No dose adjustment in mild-moderate impairment.

major: Drugs dependent on gastric pH for absorption (atazanavir, nelfinavir, erlotinib, ketoconazole, itraconazole - reduced absorption)
moderate: Clopidogrel (less effect than omeprazole, but monitor)
interactions.food: Take duodenal ulcer dose after morning meal; H. pylori regimen with food; other indications independent of food.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive secretin test for gastrinoma; may interfere with CgA levels and urine screening for THC.

monitoring: Serum magnesium before and periodically on prolonged therapy
Renal function if interstitial nephritis suspected
counsel: Swallow tablets whole; do not crush or chew

Report rash, joint pain, or new symptoms
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration
pk: Acid suppression within hours; maximal over days
~1-2 hours (effect outlasts plasma level due to irreversible binding)
Store at 25 C (77 F); excursions 15-30 C; protect from moisture
pearls: Effect outlasts plasma half-life because pump inhibition is irreversible
Take duodenal ulcer dose after the morning meal
Long-term PPI risks: hypomagnesemia, B12 deficiency, fractures, C. difficile
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered; if near the next dose, skip it. Do not double up.
overdose: No specific antidote; rabeprazole is extensively protein-bound and not readily dialyzable. Manage symptomatically and supportively.
